Trusted source installation is a local-owner operation; metadata is not executable plugin code. binding_definitions PK binding_id Same identity as catalog.bindings.binding_id/entry_id; canonical source signature UNIQUE. Source presence is occurrences(binding_id,source_id,line), with immutable per-source declarations and permission ASTs. Runtime mappings are separately keyed by binding_id plus schema_hash; unknown codecs or dispatch remain visible and noninvocable. client_binding_rules PK client_id plus binding_id client_id FK clients CASCADE; binding_id FK binding_definitions RESTRICT; schema_hash; effect CHECK deny/ask/allow; constraints_json; row_version >= 1. Exact schema-bound grants; absence denies invocation, never inventory visibility. tool_binding_aliases PK tool_id plus binding_id tool_id FK tools RESTRICT; binding_id FK binding_definitions RESTRICT; canonicalization_version; argument_mapping_hash. Generated tools, convenience plans and generic dispatch resolve the same canonical binding IDs. binding_type_schemas PK type_schema_id schema_hash UNIQUE; format_version; canonical_schema_json; validation_state. Closed typed definitions include directions, object-reference kinds, sizes and supported marshalling strategy. binding_availability read-only projection Derived from the exact fresh active device view, scoped by profile/target/user/backend/device and view/epoch/generation. Exposes binding state, all reason codes, selected schema and graph digest; stale views yield no callable rows. resolved_device_catalog also exposes types. Historical standalone cache values never authorize calls. Client grants remain independent. Catalog artifact import contract Accept a versioned SQLite catalog with equivalent JSON/JSONL export and a machine-readable source/coverage manifest. Require format version, exact source revisions and hashes, API/build applicability, schema hashes, permission evidence and mapping-state totals. Validate offline into staging and atomically publish a registry revision; no imported file supplies executable code or bypasses live Android checks. Dataset aggregation and completeness certification are separate deliverables, not implied by this design. Binding permissions metadata and validation Authorization evaluates the resolved binding IDs, not the route name. client_binding_rules is authoritative for method access; client_tool_rules can additionally restrict a convenience/entry-point tool but cannot widen a binding grant. Every required binding must be granted. Any matching global, binding or entry-point Deny wins; otherwise Ask dominates Allow and all constraints intersect. Unknown/missing binding rules deny. The UI previews canonical grants and all affected aliases when applying changes, avoiding a hidden shadow policy. Import declared Android requirements with provenance: RequiresPermission value/allOf/anyOf/conditional and read/write variants; AIDL EnforcePermission, PermissionManuallyEnforced and RequiresNoPermission where present. Absence means unknown, not no permission. Preserve the source/API version and annotation location. AppOps, runtime state and manual service checks can add requirements, so annotations are evidence, not a complete authorization oracle. [S32–S34] Publish a complete source manifest and a reconciliation report: source member count = mapped plus codec-unsupported plus schema-unknown entries, with no silent drops and exactly one mapping state per member. Runtime availability is a separate axis: a mapped member may be OS unavailable and is not counted twice. Distinguish source coverage from runtime endpoint reachability and actual authorized invocation. Android non-SDK restrictions can block reflection/JNI even when a signature is known; ordinary apps cannot enumerate or use every private system service. [S28–S31] In Avalonia, add an All bindings browser with package/interface tree, search, version/source filters and separate columns for Mapped, Codec unsupported and Schema unknown, plus a separate runtime-availability column. Show declared Android requirements, observed backend/OS access and client MCP permission in three separate fields; an Android annotation never grants a client access. Bulk permission edits preview the exact versioned member set and do not silently grant future imports. The complete inventory remains visible even when invocation is denied. Stage imports, validate recursive type limits and duplicate IDs, generate/verify dispatch artifacts, then atomically publish a new registry revision and invalidate affected approvals. A failed generator or Android marshalling gate leaves entries visible as unsupported; it must not fall back to arbitrary unvalidated parcels. Do not execute imported source code, deserialize arbitrary runtime types or silently widen a previously granted schema. Acceptance evidence Compare every source member with the published registry; round-trip overloads and parcelables; test callbacks, handles, files and one-way methods; reject malformed recursive schemas and cross-client handles. Verify generated versus generic entry points share policy, and raw access never masquerades as method-isolated permission. Test annotation allOf/anyOf/conditional/read-write handling, absent metadata as unknown, SDK/OEM version drift, missing AIDL, non- SDK denial and pagination across imports. Add real Android instrumentation after mock marshalling and policy tests. Catalog compatibility and administration API Treat the runtime catalog as a versioned data product. A companion SQLite DDL, JSON Schema and OpenAPI 3.1 contract define the machine interface. Keep catalog format version, source snapshot revision, entry revision, API version and published registry revision distinct. Stable entry IDs identify namespace plus logical qualified signature; schema/content hashes detect changed contracts. Never recycle deleted IDs or reinterpret an old schema version silently. Forward compatible catalog records Use an extensible permission expression tree: permission, allOf, anyOf, conditional, read/write, manual enforcement, declared none and unknown, each with provenance and applicability. Preserve x- properties on known semantic nodes for round-trip storage, but report them unsupported for evaluation; unknown is never equivalent to permission-free. Readers reject unsupported major formats and negotiate documented additive minor changes. Migrations retain immutable source history. Storage record Purpose registries / registry_sources / registry_entries Immutable imported source set, source revisions/hashes, format version, coverage manifest and import status. Google-imported facts are never overwritten in place. overlays Stable entry ID, base snapshot/hash, overlay revision, local additions or patches, tombstone flag and provenance. Effective entries combine the selected immutable base with validated owner changes. Storage record Purpose entry_history / registry_events / registry_outbox Actor, request ID, before/after revision, change kind, timestamp and publish result. Minimal audit; never store credentials or device-call payloads here. Separate catalog CRUD API catalog/contracts/openapi.json and catalog/API-CONTRACT.md are authoritative. There is one route family; no PATCH alias. API shape Behavior GET /v1/catalog/entries Search pinned registry/overlay view; expired cursor 410. GET /v1/catalog/entries/{entry_id} Effective entry and current cat1 ETag; conflicts visible, tombstone 410 with current ETag. POST /v1/catalog/entries Create local entry; canonical ID collision 409; Idempotency-Key required. PUT /v1/catalog/entries/{entry_id} If-Match current cat1 ETag, including conflicts/tombstones. Overlay mutation, restore or explicit rebase; no imported mutation. DELETE /v1/catalog/entries/{entry_id} If-Match; suppression/deletion tombstone; conflict requires explicit resolution first (409). GET /v1/catalog/entries/{entry_id}/h istory Immutable history and current administrative ETag for CAS. POST /v1/catalog/imports Idempotent immutable staging and validation, no active view change. GET /v1/catalog/registries/{registry_i d} Registry metadata, state and validation evidence. POST /v1/catalog/registries/{registry_i d}/publish Idempotent atomic publication of validated registry, overlay rebase/conflicts, generation increment and approval invalidation. Executable catalog DDL, configuration DDL, offline dispatch manifest generator and contract fixtures accompany this design. They specify and validate contracts; Android hosting and dispatch remain release gates requiring actual implementation/runtime evidence. Catalog administration uses a distinct authenticated admin scope and explicit owner authorization, never an ordinary device-call permission. Reuse authenticated loopback transport protections or a separately approved management transport; localhost alone is not trusted. CRUD does not grant invocation rights and exposes no client credential or permission mutation as a normal agent tool. No administration endpoint is enabled by this design document. Test source refresh with overlays, tombstone persistence, referenced-entry deletion, concurrent ETag edits, rollback, import/export round trips, unknown extension nodes, major-version rejection and no privilege gain after CRUD. Publishing altered schemas invalidates affected approvals and schema-bound grants until reevaluated. Startup device-resolved bindings, types and generic Binder execution At startup the headless service resolves a device-specific view of both bindings and types before admitting device calls. The immutable catalog remains the full inventory: unavailable, unknown, historical and future entries are retained with reasons. A filtered available view is a projection, never a replacement import or a curated catalog. Service reachability, version applicability, verified wire support, OS/backend authority and MCP client grants are separate facts. An available entry never grants invocation. Capability capture and version evidence The capability collector uses only supported metadata operations within an already configured backend's authority. It records platform SDK major/minor, separately observed SDK extension family levels, build/OEM identity and installed module/interface versions where observable. Use SDK_INT_FULL and Build's major/minor accessors on supported releases; SDK_INT alone supplies a major, not an invented minor. A release display string, targetSdkVersion, the host SDK installation and extension level24 cannot stand in for the device's platform37.2. Missing, denied or unsupported observations remain unknown with provenance. No pairing, debugging toggle, privilege escalation or phone operation is performed by this design/reference deliverable. Android's documented full-SDK fields distinguish minor releases; extension availability has a separate runtime query. Build.VERSION, Build accessors, SDK Extensions. A DeviceCapabilitySnapshot is bound to the configured connection profile, target, Android user, device/session instance, observation epoch and collection evidence. It retains unknown values instead of converting them to zero or false. Probe failure is not proof of absence. Package visibility, backend access and non-SDK restrictions can limit observations. Record authoritative absence only when the supported observation actually establishes it. Build/OEM strings identify evidence applicability; they do not prove undocumented backports. Do not collect hardware serials or credentials to populate this view. Where supported by a known adapter and permitted by the existing backend, refine service metadata with endpoint descriptor, reachability and stable AIDL interface version/hash. Use generated/proven metadata operations, bounded timeouts and exact target/profile association; do not guess transaction IDs or probe private/OEM services universally. Stable AIDL explicitly provides version/hash queries, but service discovery or successful metadata calls do not prove authorization to invoke methods. An unrecognized hash leaves the wire contract unknown; an unreachable/denied probe leaves existence uncertain instead of declaring a method removed. Stable AIDL metadata. Applicability and coherent type resolution Each source-backed binding/type variant has a versioned applicability rule and provenance. For a published lifecycle range, introduction is inclusive and removal exclusive; deprecation alone is not removal. Conditions can constrain platform major/minor, a named SDK extension family, module version, exact OEM/build evidence and supported interface version/hash. Alternatives model documented backports; constraints within one alternative must all hold. Unknown conditions cannot become true by default. The source importer must retain lifecycle metadata and historical/future declarations in the full inventory; a current-target SDK projection must not discard the only records needed to resolve an older device. Legacy or unparsed applicability stays unknown until corrected evidence is imported. The resolver selects a schema variant only when the observed facts prove it and no unresolved, potentially applicable incompatible variant remains. Conflicting variants or unrecognized semantics yield unknown with retained evidence. Availability filtering applies to types, fields/enumerants and callable bindings, not just method names. A binding's required type schemas must resolve in the same snapshot with the expected schema identities. A missing/ambiguous type yields unknown; a version-excluded required type makes the binding unavailable. Mutually recursive types resolve as one coherent graph. Hash canonical finite type graphs/references without recursive expansion, and bind the selected graph digest to dispatch schema/codec identity so a dependency change invalidates approvals even when a method name is unchanged. The view retains one result per inventory entity with selected schema hash when known, dependencies, state available/unavailable/unknown and machine-readable reasons. Preserve all inventory entries and expose source coverage gaps separately. Unknown/unreachable schemas remain visible, not callable. A known public SDK version may establish documented applicability without proving a private Binder wire layout. No type version or codec is inferred from API level alone. The authoritative editable Mermaid sources for all four diagrams are in design/sources and the portable bundle. The two inline source blocks later in this document follow the same files. Generic Binder invocation and codecs Generated tools and binding.invoke use the same canonical dispatch planner and binding.invoke policy identity. They select a binding/type graph from the active resolved view, then require a verified wire contract before marshalling. The wire registry pins endpoint/descriptor, relevant interface/OEM version/hash evidence, actual transaction code, flags/one- way semantics, request/response codec schema and handle ownership constraints. Support generated proxies or schema- driven codecs only when the complete contract is proven. Source AIDL alone does not establish generated transaction codes, runtime class resolution, parcel layout or backend authority. The generic engine validates typed arguments and exact target constraints, bounds parcel sizes, nesting, arrays, file/handle lifetimes and output, then passes the immutable plan through policy/Ask/admission. Admission rechecks catalog, resolved-view and capability epochs alongside policy and backend identity. Marshal only the admitted plan; transact through IBinderTransport; decode and validate output against the pinned graph before release. Binder death, cancellation after dispatch and uncertain outcomes never trigger automatic write replay. These are architecture responsibilities and reference contracts, not a deployed Binder engine in this phase. Known raw transactions must decode to the same binding/schema and satisfy binding.invoke plus restrictive binder.transact rules. When schema/codec proof is missing, typed invocation stays unsupported; an explicitly authorized raw low-level operation remains a separate broad service authority with closed connection/descriptor/code/flag/handle bounds. A raw grant cannot substitute for a known binding grant. Android's actual authority still decides whether the transaction can execute. No target application must embed instrumentation for generic ADB screen/tap control; optional Avalonia Android Runtime/Protocol stays a separate adapter, not desktop Server/Kestrel. Resolved view and policy-bound generic Binder dispatch Rendered with Pele 1.10.0 from the editable Mermaid source in the portable bundle. Atomic activation, invalidation and refresh Capture facts under a capability epoch; build the entire binding/type result set privately against pinned catalog and overlay generations. Validate complete inventory membership, variant identities and type dependencies before sealing. Activate one immutable snapshot pointer in a single transaction only if catalog, profile/target/device identity, capability epoch and expected view generation still match. A failed build/CAS retains the previous snapshot as historical evidence; it never exposes a partial mixture. Snapshot IDs/ETags and pagination cursors bind the complete view and generation. An available row cannot depend on an unavailable, unknown or mismatched required type in that same view. Startup, reconnect/device replacement, boot/session or Android-user change, OS/build/OEM update, SDK extension/Mainline/module change, supported interface version/hash or reachability change, backend capability change and catalog/type/overlay publication invalidate affected active views and pending approvals. Mark the view stale immediately; no new device call may use it. Keep the full catalog accessible and distinguish Resolving/Stale from MCP listener health and ADB connection health. Refresh from supported backend events, startup/reconnect and explicit owner requests; this introduces no app-specific monitoring scheduler. Where a platform cannot notify a change, revalidate the relevant observations at call admission rather than treating cached availability as timeless authority. Existing live permission/policy checks remain mandatory and separate. The executable device resolver/store is an offline reference using fixture observations, with no Android/HTTP service or real probes. The API contract accepts refresh requests for configured targets but never accepts a remote caller's asserted facts or availability as authority. Current-view reads return a small header/status; entries are paginated at the administration API maximum500, pinned to the complete immutable snapshot. The full snapshot payload is internal storage/reference data, not one unbounded HTTP response. The existing immutable import/local override/CAS contract remains in force; user edits cannot manufacture observed device evidence. Namespace/package file re-sharding remains a proposal. Source projection, capture epoch and storage contract The executable producer now retains all versioned SDK-index records, including historical/future entries. A native current-target flag is used only for current annotation/JVM-equivalence lookup; it is never a claim about a running device or installed SDK extensions. The catalog projection keeps immutable source declarations intact while enriching derived registry entries with proven same-snapshot TypeReference IDs and versioned inventory variants. Each variant uses the shared dispatch contract digest and pins its containing/argument/return/structured-field type schemas. SDK lifecycle ranges and declared extension alternatives are source-backed; a standalone occurrence labeled37.2 emits platform_point: [37,2]. Matching that point is positive applicability evidence; older, newer or unknown minors remain unknown with PLATFORM_APPLICABILITY_UNPROVEN. A source point never fabricates a removed bound. Conflicting explicit since/sdk0 evidence is quarantined with its raw lifecycle metadata. Unknown or ambiguous types/lifetimes remain visible, and a proven version exclusion remains unavailable even when another schema fact is unknown. The complete registry_inventory is exported with a versioned manifest and independently reconciled against Entry hashes, source evidence, type hashes and stream bytes; absent or partial legacy inventories cannot initialize a startup view. Facts are captured with capability_epoch and observed_at. The resolver rejects epoch relabeling; publication also verifies the exact facts hash, scope and current epoch. A non-authoritative positive module/interface observation remains unknown. Malformed intervals are quarantined with APPLICABILITY_MALFORMED without discarding unrelated inventory. Every available root/type graph has graph_digest over the sorted transitive root/type(entry_id,contract_hash) closure; publication recomputes it. The final schema_hash is SHA256 of canonical {schema_format:closure3, contract_hash:C, graph_digest:G}. A dependent type change therefore invalidates prior binding/schema grants without recursive hash cycles. Raw lifecycle/annotation header text stays in provenance and does not affect the semantic type digest. This is schema identity, not proof of a Binder codec or permission. Catalog inventory DeviceResolution2.1.0 adds explicit point evidence. Resolved DeviceView3.0.0 requires the inventory digest, base contract_hash, transitive graph_digest and final schema_hash; it supersedes earlier unimplemented resolved drafts. Older draft snapshots remain historical and cannot be activated silently. Entry1.1 and catalog storage1.2 remain separate contracts; OpenAPI specification version is1.4.0. Offline generated aliases can consume the fresh trusted-store view and use exactly the selected generic schema and graph digest; the complete inventory remains discoverable. They remain default-deny and unavailable for execution until live authority and verified wire/codec contracts pass the shared admission gate. The executable configuration DDL stores immutable facts, staged/sealed device_views and device_view_entries, a scoped generation/epoch/catalog/overlay CAS pointer and append-only invalidation reasons. A catalog-pinned inventory_sha256 and expected_inventory_count reject substituted and partial views. The digest hashes the complete canonical sorted inventory JSONL, including variant identities. The trusted loader checks this digest before sealing immutable inventory sets/members. Publication recomputes resolution from the pinned inventory and exact facts, rejecting altered membership, selected contracts, dependencies or states. SQLite also checks complete membership and selected base-contract/type pins. Core SQLite does not supply SHA256; content hashing belongs to the checked loader. The strong dv2 status ETag includes the inventory digest as well as scope/generation/epoch/catalog/overlay pins. SQLite JSON/normalized columns agree; active/pinned snapshots cannot be collected. binding_availability is a read-only fresh projection, not an independent cache authority. Versioned binding_wire_contracts stores interface version/hash, transaction code, flags/oneway and codec/proof evidence separately from existence. device_view_storage is an offline transaction reference; Android collectors, Binder execution, HTTP/MCP service deployment and actual OS permission grants remain runtime integration gates. Effective overlays, semantic identity and bounded execution The startup coordinator uses effective_device_inventory to capture the selected immutable registry and all local overlays in one read transaction. Full inventory includes local additions and tombstones as well as suppressed/conflicting rows. Catalog exposure state is separate from version existence and per-client grants: suppressing a type does not claim it ceased to exist, but known typed dispatch through that type is denied. New local entries without imported applicability evidence remain unknown. Overridden fields update the enclosing structured type contract and dependent schema closure. Capture pins registry/overlay generations, local revisions and canonical effective document hashes; generation changes invalidate the view. Generated aliases and generic/known-raw plans use the same selected schema, type graph and current effective metadata. A stale metadata/document pin rejects even when a metadata-only edit leaves the semantic schema hash unchanged. Semantic contract format3 includes normalized type parameters, declared supertypes, parameter directions, known wire type annotations, inherited oneway and HIDL result types. Type-reference proof prose, source revisions and raw lifecycle headers stay outside semantic shape hashes. Unknown syntax, generic instantiation, imports and wire layouts remain explicit. Missing or unknown Entry.kind cannot be guessed into an invocable binding. Structured fields/enumerants and type nodes remain in inventory, with method aliases generated only for actual binding kinds. The full offline Python checkpoint projected/resolved 799,527 historical008 entries using fixture37.2 facts: 432,590 available and366,937 unknown, including392,959 bindings and39,631 types with positive applicability evidence. This is neither an observed device nor a new catalog publication. Resolution/validation took565.6seconds and the whole desktop probe peaked at4.30GiB; it does not meet the headless runtime memory targets below. The preserved checkpoint predates the subsequent format3/overlay delta. Runtime design therefore uses indexed SQLite staging and bounded batches rather than materializing all documents: evaluate version variants, maintain available dependency adjacency and reverse worklists, traverse coherent type closures with bounded scratch storage, stream canonical hash input, then seal and activate the complete snapshot. The executable DDL includes device_type_edges and reverse indexes. UI/listener health remains separate from resolving readiness; no call is admitted through a partial/stale view. Android latency/memory measurements remain a release gate. No deployment, device/security change or source-corpus completeness claim is made by these additions. Round011 independently assessed design95/95, contracts93/93, extractor94/92 and overall93/84 (NOT_READY). It verified the prior artifact fixes and found point-applicability/membership defects plus lower-severity parser/contract gaps. The corrected candidate now has explicit point evidence, digest-pinned membership and transitive schema identity; these later changes require fresh independent review; no98/98 agreement is claimed. 19 Acceptance tests and delivery sequence Build mock first, then prove the Android boundary. Passing policy tests alone does not establish compatibility, permissions, lifecycle reliability or store eligibility. Every gate produces retained test evidence and a pinned dependency manifest; there is no implementation claim in this proposal. Test area Acceptance evidence Policy properties Unknown client/tool/schema, empty scopes and unknown constraint keys deny. Global deny dominates. Ask never widens scope. Output fields and pagination remain constrained. Approval binding Changing any argument, target, output field, credential epoch, policy revision or schema invalidates approval. Concurrent double use admits once. Expiry survives clock rollback; restart invalidates all approvals. Authorization races Barrier tests race Apply/Revoke with admission and SSE emission. No request admitted after the revocation commit uses old authority. In flight outcomes are labeled accurately. Identity and transport Spoofed clientInfo or package header cannot choose another principal. Missing auth, cross client session IDs, hostile Origin/Host, reconnect and oversized JSON are rejected. Endpoint identity A fake listener on the old port cannot obtain a credential in the preferred paired TLS profile. Compatibility clients and any lower assurance mode are explicitly documented. SQLite durability Constraint failures roll back all rule changes. Conflict edits never overwrite silently. Crash injection covers migration, policy commit, admission and outbox delivery; no permissive fallback. Android integration Release build invokes actual public API and a test AIDL service. Test runtime permission denial/revocation, WRITE_SETTINGS loss, brightness mode races, sensor cleanup, service death, signer/version change and Keystore invalidation. Lifecycle Test rotation, activity recreation, backgrounding, process kill, force stop, reboot, device lock and approved foreground service mode across supported Android versions and vendor devices. UI accessibility Phone and tablet, large text, screen reader and keyboard navigation work. Deny/Ask/Allow remains distinct from OS status. Dirty drafts, conflicts, revocation and expiry are understandable. Privacy and performance Automated secret canaries never appear in logs/exports. Limits stop queue growth. Measure request overhead, DB contention, memory and battery before setting service level targets. Delivery sequence and exit criteria 1. Compatibility spike: prove Avalonia 12 Android release build, persistent/boot service, HTTP host, MCP baseline, SQLite, Keystore and full-source registry generation. Exit with supported device/client matrix and exact pinned versions. 2. Security core: implement policy shared by generated/generic/raw paths, marshalling, handle ownership, approvals, transactional edits and fake adapters. Exit with deterministic race and property tests passing. 3. Vertical slice: pair one MCP client and a self-ADB profile, read screen.state and issue one authorized input.tap against a test app. Verify image coordinates, stale-reference rejection, direct mode, unknown outcomes and configured Allow versus Ask. 4. Complete generic capabilities: validate settings/files/sensors and optional partner AIDL, per-client logging, external- host forwarding and any enabled Avalonia runtime adapter. Exit after restore, lifecycle and security gates; app- specific workflows remain outside the bridge. 20 Decisions and source references Decisions to settle before implementation Decision Recommended starting point Exposed surface Complete declared SDK/AIDL/protocol inventory with generated and generic invocation; screen.state/input.tap and native wrappers are conveniences, not a curated limit. Client authentication Manual paired bearer profile for compatible on device agents; preferred pinned loopback TLS. Add standards based authorization only when required by target clients. Decision Recommended starting point Runtime availability Persistent foreground MCP service independent of UI, optional boot start, truthful AppBar/status notification, restart recovery and explicit OS-blocked states. Android support floor Set after compatibility spike and intended device inventory. Test real supported devices; do not infer support from successful desktop tests. Privacy level Local minimal audit and disabled client restore. Decide whether sensitive scope identifiers require encrypted storage and exports. Partner Binder integration Native Binder needs a known contract. Arbitrary-app UI control uses authorized ADB; optional Avalonia.RemoteControl requires an instrumented target and extra integration gates. Editable source follows. sequenceDiagram participant C as Client participant P as Policy participant V as Device view participant U as Owner participant G as Gate participant A as Adapter C->>P: Authenticated call P->>V: Pin binding types and capability epoch P->>P: Validate plan opt Ask configured P->>U: Bound request U->>P: Decision break Denied or expired P-->>C: No dispatch end end P->>G: Plan and revisions G->>G: Recheck and audit G->>V: Reject stale or changed device view G->>A: Typed operation A-->>P: Result or unknown P->>P: Filter and bounded log P-->>C: Response Note over G,A: No replay of uncertain taps Remediation contract precedence This revision addresses the recovered design/contract findings; the source-coverage finding remains open and is tracked in the latest ledger. Stable source-signature IDs are shared across imported occurrences and local overrides; registry schema/permission changes are revisions, not new random identities. No universal OEM/private introspection is promised: unsupported declarations and schemas remain discoverable with evidence and reasons. Catalog metadata is distinct from OS authority and MCP grants. catalog/API-CONTRACT.md defines all CRUD states, CAS and cursor rules; catalog/bridge-config.sql makes configuration invariants executable; catalog/tooling/policy_reference.py and dispatch_manifest.py provide offline contract fixtures, not a running bridge. Existing section diagrams remain editable Mermaid; Pele 1.10.0 rendering is a separate packaging check. The catalog SQL and bridge-config.sql can coexist in the same app-private SQLite database; the offline catalog may also be distributed as an immutable standalone file. A serving administration service must use one transactional database for active registry, overlays, policy epochs and audit/outbox, avoiding cross-database atomicity claims. registry_entries stores immutable (registry_id, entry_id) variants; effective_entries selects only active_registry. Publication switches that pointer and increments registry_generation atomically. Raw unknown calls consult explicit client_raw_grants keyed by connection/descriptor and bounded transaction codes/flags, with ordinary binding grants unable to widen that authority. The raw grant DDL is client_raw_grants(client_id, connection_id, descriptor, code_min, code_max, flags_mask, contract_hash, effect, constraints_json, row_version). constraints_json is scope-only (allowed_targets, allowed_handles, allowed_displays, max_items); connection, descriptor, inclusive code range, flags mask, contract hash and effect are authoritative SQL columns. Empty scope sets deny, and there is no implicit wildcard. Resolve known transactions before checking raw grants: a raw grant can never substitute for a known binding rule. Unknown raw access is a broad authority with explicitly limited observability; ask/allow is available only within every stated bound. Canonical permission entry points and retained unknown metadata Generated per-binding MCP tool names and binding.invoke share the single policy tool_id binding.invoke . The protocol alias name is stored separately in tool_binding_aliases.alias_name; tools/client_tool_rules represent the shared policy entry point, not hundreds of thousands of independent shadow permission rows. Editing a generated alias in the UI edits its canonical client_binding_rules row. Convenience wrappers have their own restrictive entry-point rules in addition to every required binding grant. A known binder.transact call must also satisfy binding.invoke and its canonical binding rules, then the extra binder.transact restriction; unknown raw calls use their separate explicit raw grants and binder.transact rule. Equal route constraints produce equal decisions; an extra route-specific restriction can only narrow access. PermissionExpression accepts only known op values. Future x- properties on known nodes are retained; an unrecognized semantic node is quarantined as a known unknown wrapper with reason plus exact parsed JSON value in x-raw-node (and required_semantics as appropriate), never interpreted as permission-free. Original imported bytes remain in versioned evidence. Unsupported major versions stay unsupported for invocation. settings.brightness.get reports the actual observed signed32-bit rawValue without clamping, plus withinDocumentedRange and the cited documentedRange1..255. An out-of-range observation (including0 on a differing device) is returned with an anomaly flag, rather than fabricated as a valid documented setting or rejected by the output range. The write policy remains bounded to the documented range with default16..240; no automatic mode change is implied. Native availability uses the reserved target_key platform:local; app/runtime targets must exist in target_app_profiles. Audit retention is a separate authenticated local-owner maintenance transaction: set bridge_config.audit_retention_authorized=1, perform bounded retention deletes, append maintenance audit evidence, reset the flag to0 before commit. Startup resets a stale flag before admitting calls. No remote catalog or MCP device endpoint can enable maintenance or issue SQL. Optional client-log purge remains separate from mandatory audit retention. permission_reader.read is the offline future semantic-node reader: unknown operators become validated unknown wrappers with x-raw-node, preserving the parsed JSON value; original lexical bytes remain in immutable source/import evidence. Known malformed ASTs are rejected. Generated extractor AST validation remains strict. No extension/raw node is interpreted as authority. Runtime/HTTP reader integration remains a release gate for bridge implementation. Offline catalog source occurrences are occurrences(binding_id,source_id,line), joined to binding_declarations at the same key. The separate bridge-config.sql projection is binding_occurrences(binding_id,source_id,locator,record_hash,provenance_json): its locator is line:<positive physical source line> for an imported declaration, record_hash is that declaration's record_sha256, and provenance_json retains the source evidence. This projection shares IDs and never replaces the immutable catalog occurrences. External annotation_evidence uses its own source_id/locator key. Every new owner CRUD mutation persists its reason in append- only entry_history_reasons(entry_id,revision,reason), in the same transaction as entry_history; HistoryEvent joins and returns it. Legacy/system events without supplied justification omit the optional reason rather than fabricate one. One protocol alias may require multiple canonical bindings. tool_binding_aliases stores one row per (alias_name,binding_id), while all rows sharing an alias_name must use one policy tool_id. Generated binding aliases share binding.invoke; convenience plans additionally require every referenced binding grant and their own restrictive entry-point rule. The alias constraint never replaces per-binding or OS authority checks. Device capacity and latency acceptance budgets These are engineering acceptance targets, not claimed measurements. The reference deployment profile is64-bit Android35+ with8GiB RAM and128GB storage. Broader support must meet the same budgets and all platform gates. The measured release010 reference SQLite catalog is10,276,548,608 bytes (about9.57GiB), SHA-256 3eb7a2d1ae0fdeeb2743aa1814fe3bf9d2ac5f167d3dec1bde3ac900c0497eb7; evidence/catalog-size-release010.json identifies the owner final manifest hash and own stable file-size check. It contains44,397 imported sources in that frozen checkpoint; this does not establish global coverage. The newer inventory projection and derived device views may increase storage, so preflight uses actual active/incoming bytes and configured view quotas rather than this historical reference size. Raw source archives and JSON audit exports stay off-device. Keep the entire admitted inventory, never a curated subset to meet a budget. Before accepting an atomic catalog replacement, require additional free space >= incoming_catalog_bytes + bounded_staging_scratch_bytes + remaining_configured_log_and_config_quota +1GiB safety reserve. Conservatively budget scratch at incoming_catalog_bytes. With an existing active catalog of the same release010 reference size, this requires at least21GiB additional free space plus the configured quota; the total peak catalog footprint, including that already allocated active copy, rounds up to30GiB plus the quota. Do not count the existing active file twice when comparing against reported free space. Retain the previous immutable catalog until validation and pointer publication succeed; insufficient space yields CATALOG_CAPACITY_REQUIRED and no partial publication. Bridge health reports catalog readiness separately from listener and ADB health. The headless service target is <=256MiB idle RSS and <=384MiB peak excluding OS-owned graphics buffers, SQLite page cache <=32MiB, one bounded on-demand capture at a time, and no preload of all catalog documents. All-bindings UI lists use indexed queries and virtualization: default100 entries per page, hard maximum1000 through application query interfaces over local SQLite; the administration API remains capped at500 per request. Device targets: p95 <=150ms for a metadata page/query, <=25ms for local policy lookup, <=250ms for an owner permission commit, and <=2s to first management view. Backend/ADB/network dispatch latency is measured separately and never hidden in the policy number. Validate these budgets on each supported device/OS using the complete registry, cold/warm caches and the configured maximum client/rule/log quotas before claiming runtime readiness. Budget failures block that device profile or publication; they do not justify dropping inventory rows or claiming measured feasibility from host tests. No device benchmark or phone operation was performed in this deliverable phase. Derived device views have a configured byte quota and bounded history. Pin snapshots used by admitted calls and live cursors; collect only unreferenced expired derived snapshots through trusted maintenance. Never delete immutable catalog/source or audit evidence for view-cache pressure. If a complete view cannot be staged within quota, retain the old snapshot as stale and report capacity failure; no partial activation. Package extension_level metadata is the SDK package's base extension metadata, not an observation of the running device. Catalog-driven callbacks and bounded event delivery This extension records the user's callback and functional tool-group requirements. It is a design and catalog contract, with offline reference validation planned below; it does not claim a deployed subscription service or complete callback extraction. It preserves the complete inventory, startup device resolution, existing authority gates, Avalonia12 management UI, headless service, SQLite configuration, ADB convenience operations and optional Android RemoteControl integration. Callback inventory and evidence Every imported binding and type receives a callback-classification disposition: proven callback, candidate, proven non- callback, or unknown with a reason. The global index retains unclassified and unreachable records. Extract all source- declared callback interfaces, listener/delegate types and abstract callback classes, their inherited methods, and methods accepting or returning them. Binder one-way syntax proves call semantics; a name ending in Listener or Callback alone proves only a candidate. An ordinary synchronous Binder interface can also be a callback. Registration patterns inferred from names remain candidates until supported by signature, documentation, annotations, implementation direction or explicit reviewed source evidence. HIDL generates clauses describe RPC completion results and must not automatically become durable subscriptions. Each versioned CallbackDescriptor records stable callback-type and method IDs; normalized type and method schema hashes; declaration/source locator and immutable import hash; platform, extension, module and interface applicability; role and confidence; argument direction and zero-based formal argument position; registration, replacement and cleanup binding IDs; and registration-token/receiver identity mapping. A relationship may be many-to-many or unresolved. Overloads use canonical IDs, never names alone. Registration/cleanup pair evidence must establish token ownership and argument mapping; unsupported, ambiguous and unknown cases remain searchable. No absent evidence is converted into an Android availability claim. Callback metadata follows immutable imports plus provenance-qualified local overrides, revisions, history and ETag/CAS rules used by other catalog entries. Overrides cannot manufacture runtime wire proof or Android authority. The device-resolved view includes callback types and the coherent closure of event argument types, response types, registration results and cleanup arguments. Callback roles are independent from existence, reachability, verified codec/wire contract, OS authority and MCP client grants. The same canonical permission plan covers generated, generic and raw invocation, callback registration, event reception, local reply policy and cleanup. A generic raw transaction cannot bypass that plan by supplying a callback object as an opaque argument. Unknown callback ABI, return semantics, cleanup mapping or sender-verification requirements yield an explicit unsupported reason for registration; their source records remain in the inventory. Invocation and subscription lifecycle The existing binding.invoke tool adds an optional callback_bindings array. Each item identifies the formal parameter position, CallbackDescriptor ID/revision/hash, selected callback method IDs, delivery policy, retention limits, lease, and a bounded local response policy when needed. Supplying arbitrary executable code, an external callback URL or an untyped Binder object is not supported. The resolved registration/cleanup/type/wire contracts and the client's current grants are checked before proxy creation. The backend validates the callback sender using its supported UID/endpoint capability checks; inability to establish the required sender boundary is explicit, not inferred from a client-supplied identity. Registration is a bounded operation with one final tools/call response. The response includes registration outcome (active, failed or outcome_unknown), the ordinary invocation result, and subscription descriptors. An active descriptor contains subscription_id, stream_epoch, events_uri, initial application cursor, cancellation handle, lease expiry, effective buffer quotas and schema pins. The URI and handle are opaque locators, not bearer authority. Registration idempotency keys are scoped to client principal, credential epoch, target/user/backend epoch and exact contract hash; reuse with different arguments conflicts. If a device transaction may have executed but its reply is lost, persist outcome_unknown and do not blindly register again. Callbacks arriving during registration enter a provisional bounded journal and become visible only with an active registration; a failed or uncertain registration retains a restricted diagnostic disposition and cleanup obligation. The persistent headless service owns CallbackBroker and the journal; closing the Avalonia window does not stop it. Subscription records and retained events may survive transport reconnect and bridge restart. Android callback registrations generally do not survive bridge/device/backend death. Recovery marks those registrations orphaned, records the reason and attempts only verified cleanup/reconciliation; it does not claim a durable live Binder proxy or automatically replay a side-effecting registration. Lifecycle states are registering, active, cancelling, closed, orphaned and outcome_unknown. Every transition has a revision and reason. Terminal states cannot be silently reactivated; a new registration gets a new stream epoch/handle. An explicit callback.cancel tool performs idempotent cancellation and verified unregister/dispose using the recorded token mapping. Its result distinguishes locally closed delivery from confirmed remote cleanup and cleanup_unknown. Binder death, target uninstall, device/backend epoch change, permission revocation and lease expiry invalidate delivery. Authorization is rechecked on reads and before event publication; revocation immediately suppresses payload access and queues least-privileged recorded cleanup. It never authorizes an arbitrary new operation on behalf of a revoked client. Transport disconnect alone is not cancellation. A configured lease/grace bounds disconnected retention; a client must explicitly renew within its authorized maximum. resources/unsubscribe stops resource-update hints only; it does not unregister the Android callback. Deactivating a tool group does not orphan subscriptions: the bootstrap cancel/status tools remain available. MCP2025-11-25 transport contract The interoperable baseline uses standard MCP resources. The server advertises resources.subscribe support. The invocation result returns a resource link and events_uri such as android-callback://subscription-id/events. The client may subscribe to that exact URI with resources/subscribe. A coalescible notifications/resources/updated notification contains the URI only. The client then uses resources/read on the advertised URI template android-callback://subscription-id/events{?cursor,limit,max_bytes} to obtain a finite application/json journal page. The no-query URI reads the earliest retained page. A page contains events, next_cursor, has_more, oldest_retained_cursor, terminal state and any explicit loss range. The implementation validates and canonicalizes the URI, checks ownership, enforces fixed maxima, and never treats path/query values as SQL or file paths. Cursors bind subscription, stream epoch, principal/credential scope and retention revision; they are integrity-protected and opaque. An expired cursor returns cursor_expired with the available retention boundary, never a fabricated contiguous replay. On StreamableHTTP, standard notifications can arrive on the client's GET SSE stream; on stdio they are ordinary MCP notification messages. A POST tools/call may use SSE while registration runs, then produces its single final JSON-RPC response and normally terminates that request stream. Callback events do not become additional final responses or indefinite progress updates. Clients lacking resource-subscription support can explicitly perform bounded reads; this is caller-driven retrieval, not a bridge business-monitoring scheduler. A resource link is not a promise that every MCP host automatically subscribes or inserts payloads into agent context. Direct payload SSE is optional and disabled by default. A future implementation may expose a separately authenticated subscription stream, or a fully documented mutually negotiated experimental extension. It must advertise its exact transport, authorization, schema, limits and cancellation rules and retain the standard resource-read fallback. No custom method is represented as an MCP standard notification. The baseline requires no extension and does not depend on an LLM host implementing one. Transport Last-Event-ID is an MCP stream-replay token, subject to session/stream routing and server retention; it is distinct from the callback application's journal cursor. Reconnecting transport may replay a resource-update hint but does not advance or acknowledge journal consumption. Client deduplication uses (subscription_id, stream_epoch, sequence), not the SSE event ID. Standard progress tokens stop with the original operation and are not used as permanent subscription channels. These are application patterns composed from the pinned standard, not new MCP guarantees. Sources: MCP transports, MCP resources, MCP tools, MCP progress. Event envelope, bounds and synchronous replies Each accepted event has subscription_id, stream_epoch, a decimal-string sequence, event_id, callback method ID, immutable schema hash, registration correlation ID, observed UTC timestamp, monotonic capture offset and either typed payload, scoped payload-resource reference, or typed error. Sequence order is assigned atomically when appending within one subscription across concurrent Binder threads; it is not a claim about physical ordering across threads, callbacks or subscriptions. Replay is at-least-once for retained accepted journal events; Android source delivery and crashes before durable acceptance are not exactly-once guarantees. Source omissions and known loss ranges are exposed. No acknowledgement deletes another consumer's events; any explicit acknowledgement is consumer-scoped and retention still honors the shared bounded quota. Default proposed limits are 256 events or1MiB per subscription (whichever comes first), 64KiB inline event, 64 events/128KiB per read, 10-minute journal retention, 5-minute renewable lease and a global per-client journal quota. These are configurable engineering defaults pending Android measurement, not published platform limits. Admission reserves space for terminal/loss metadata and applies the lower server/client quota. Payload-resource references consume the same quota and cannot bypass it. The default overflow policy closes delivery and reports buffer_overflow; optional drop_oldest/drop_newest is explicitly chosen and reports exact lost sequence ranges. Coalescing requires semantic evidence and opt-in, otherwise it can erase meaningful events. Oversized/unsupported payloads produce a bounded typed error or scoped resource, never silent truncation. Binder threads release native resources promptly; no producer waits for a remote consumer to drain the buffer. Disk-full marks durability_failed and closes the stream; it does not acknowledge a durable append. Reads and resource hints do not log payloads by default. For return-valued synchronous callbacks, the reply path is local. Registration must select an allowlisted typed constant or bounded deterministic handler with method-specific evidence that the response is valid. It must also declare a monotonic deadline no longer than the verified caller allowance and an approved typed timeout/error/default policy. There is no universal safe default or universal Binder deadline. Unknown deadlines/default semantics or unbounded handlers mean unsupported_synchronous_reply. The event may still report the locally selected reply and reason after completion. A remote agent may update a future policy only by a separate authorized CAS mutation; no current synchronous call blocks on network, model inference, resource reads or agent approval. Void/one-way callbacks enqueue and return promptly; HIDL RPC completion adapters retain their finite call correlation and are not mislabeled as subscriptions. SQLite stores subscription metadata/revisions, exact contract pins, lease state, journal records keyed by subscription/epoch/sequence, per-client quotas, cleanup obligations and bounded replay cursors. Event-journal persistence is functional data storage, distinct from configurable call logging. Both use app-private storage, owner- controlled retention and per-client disclosure. Logging can record correlation/size/errors without payload; sensitive payload logging requires that client's explicit configuration. No callback can execute an app-specific decision workflow in the bridge. Callback architecture Rendered with Pele 1.10.0 from the editable Mermaid source in the portable bundle. Callback registration and delivery Rendered with Pele 1.10.0 from the editable Mermaid source in the portable bundle. Small functional tool groups and job-based discovery The complete catalog remains available, but an agent starts with a small stable bootstrap tool set: android.groups.discover, android.groups.describe, android.groups.set_active, binding.invoke, callback.status and callback.cancel. Generic invocation accepts canonical IDs and validates the exact contract. Full schema enumeration is an explicit bounded operation. The management UI provides functional groups, current activation, estimated context cost, required grants, availability reasons and per-client logging controls alongside the existing client configuration. Discovery can locate unknown/unavailable capabilities without granting access to their invocation or revealing another client's private overrides/configuration. Groups represent a small coherent job capability, such as display brightness read/write, location subscription lifecycle, audio volume control, package metadata inspection or rendered-screen input. These are illustrative group shapes, not a curated allowlist or a claim that these source mappings are implemented. A group is neither one Java package nor an entire Android subsystem. Every entry has one or more provenance-qualified group memberships or an explicit unassigned reason and remains searchable by canonical ID/type/source. Shared types and permissions live in the global index, not duplicated as conflicting per-group definitions. Do not semantically re-shard the physical catalog as part of this design change. FunctionalGroup records stable group_id, revision, content hash, title, bounded description, searchable labels, immutable import provenance and override lineage; canonical binding memberships; required type closure; dependencies and optional related groups; lifecycle invariants; and measured serialized descriptor bytes plus an explicitly labeled token estimate. Registration/unregistration/replacement and token/type dependencies form one atomic lifecycle unit. A group cannot advertise registration while hiding the required cleanup operation. Unknown cleanup remains visible and blocks activation of that unsafe registration unit. Large coherent units can stay generic-invoke-only with an oversize reason; they cannot be partially loaded to satisfy a context budget. Dependencies use immutable revisions/hashes, cycle validation and bounded closure; unresolved dependency metadata is explicit. android.groups.discover accepts a task/job description, optional capability/backend/device constraints, availability and permission filters, maximum groups, maximum response bytes and optional estimated-token budget. The server deterministically searches normalized labels, descriptions, canonical symbols and source-derived functional annotations, then ranks stable ties by group ID. Optional semantic ranking may improve relevance only; the deterministic index remains usable without an LLM, and ranking never changes grants or device authority. Descriptions, user overrides and job text are untrusted data, never instructions executed by the bridge. The result returns ranked small summaries, IDs/revisions/hashes, relevant capability IDs, dependency counts, applicability/permission status with reasons and a scoped continuation cursor. It omits all full tool/type schemas. Bounded ranking is over the full index, not a preselected functional subset. Search bounds may stop work with an explicit partial-search flag and cursor; the response never claims exhaustive job suitability when a search was truncated. For example, “observe location changes, then stop” can return a location-subscription group summary including register/unregister/callback lifecycle and location payload-type dependency. The agent describes that group for exact contracts, asks to activate the coherent unit within its budget, invokes registration, consumes its bounded resource journal and cancels. The bridge makes no travel, app-specific or timing decision. If permission is denied or applicability unknown, discovery reports that status and activation cannot grant the missing authority. Activation, concurrency and host compatibility Interest/activation is scoped to authenticated client, credential epoch and MCP session. It is separate from per-client permission grants and from the device's resolved availability. android.groups.set_active submits the entire desired group- ID/revision/hash set plus expected view ETag and byte/token-estimate budgets. The transaction resolves dependencies and types, checks current catalog/device/policy epochs, serializes the proposed descriptors and atomically accepts the complete set or returns a conflict/budget/unknown-dependency error without partial activation. Deactivation uses the same CAS operation. Stable tool names include canonical binding identity; names cannot be reused for different contracts after refresh. View cursors bind owner/session, activation revision, catalog/device/policy epochs and expiry. Foreign, stale or mismatched cursors are rejected. No client sees another session's activation or private mappings. There are two explicit presentation modes. The default portable mode exposes only the stable bootstrap tools through tools/list; active groups supply bounded schema manifests for generic binding.invoke. This prevents bridge-side eager exposure of thousands of generated tools even if a host exhausts tools/list pagination. A host that supports an explicitly negotiated group-view feature may opt into dynamic aliases for its active groups. In that mode, tools/list enumerates exactly the current session's coherent activated aliases plus bootstrap tools, with bounded pages and a revision-scoped cursor. Changes emit the standard notifications/tools/list_changed when advertised. This custom session-view feature and its cache contract are documented as an opt-in application feature, not a standard MCP selective-context guarantee. Unknown hosts use portable mode. Pagination alone cannot prevent an eager host fetching every page. list_changed support also does not guarantee that a host refreshes its cache or evicts old schemas from the model context. The bridge can bound its response sizes and exposed set; actual host context usage is a measured integration property. A client unable to apply dynamic changes retains bootstrap/generic-invoke mode and explicitly fetches only the required manifest pages. Token estimates are labeled with estimator/version and never treated as an exact host-model tokenizer budget. A strict UTF-8 serialized-byte maximum is enforced independently, including descriptions and dependency/type metadata; a single oversize unit is refused for alias loading. Catalog import, override revision, group mapping edits, device/backend change and permission revocation invalidate the matching caches. In-flight calls pin their admitted complete contract/type/policy plan. A harmless activation view change alone does not invalidate an already admitted call or live callback handle; a contract, capability or authority change revalidates or rejects it with stale_contract/revoked/epoch_changed. No cached schema grants continuing authority. Subscriptions retain explicit cancellation/status through bootstrap even when their group is removed. Safe descriptor- only group changes may preserve handles when their exact registration, callback and cleanup pins are unchanged; incompatible changes require explicit cancellation/re-registration, not silent retargeting. Management, CRUD and component responsibilities The catalog CRUD contract adds immutable imported CallbackDescriptor and FunctionalGroup resources, append-only evidence, separate local overlays and CAS history. GET/list support bounded filters and stable cursors. Owner- authenticated PUT/PATCH/DELETE affects local mappings or tombstones; imported evidence is never rewritten. Deleting a referenced group mapping is rejected while an active view pins it or creates a new revision used only after explicit activation; existing evidence remains retrievable by revision. Activation is a session operation, not an import mutation. Client permission changes keep their existing independent grant API and immediately invalidate affected admission/cache epochs. Avalonia12 presents a functional-group editor and searchable unassigned queue, source/default versus local override provenance, dependency and callback pair inspection, context budget previews, active session views and subscription status/cancellation. UI edits use the same CAS APIs. It distinguishes source evidence, device applicability, permission denial and current activation. The persistent service remains operational independently of this UI, retains its running indicator and separate MCP/ADB health, and applies existing Android foreground-service and boot limits. Component Responsibility ICallbackCatalogClassifier Exhaustive disposition and evidence-qualified role/pair/type metadata; unknowns retained. ICallbackAdmissionPlanner Pin coherent registration/event/reply/cleanup contracts and apply canonical policy, OS and wire gates. ICallbackProxyAdapter Verify supported sender boundary, decode typed callbacks and provide bounded local synchronous replies. ICallbackBroker / ISubscriptionJournal Atomic ordered append, quotas, leases, replay, loss/terminal markers and cleanup obligations in the headless service. IMcpCallbackResourceAdapter Standard subscribe/update/read URI mapping, exact authorization and bounded pages; no custom standard notifications. IFunctionalGroupIndex Full-catalog searchable memberships/unassigned records and deterministic job ranking. IGroupActivationPlanner Complete dependency closure, serialized-byte budgeting and session-scoped CAS view activation. IMcpToolViewAdapter Stable bootstrap fallback; opt-in dynamic aliases and standard list_changed notification.
